issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: The engine revs up but the van doesn't speed up to match, shifts come late or not at all, or the van struggles to move. The check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in this van wears its internal clutches, especially with high mileage, heavy loads or old fluid. GM issued service bulletins for slipping, no-shift and overheating conditions on this transmission.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and smell (burnt fluid is a bad sign). If it is slipping, drive gently and get a transmission diagnosis soon; continuing to drive can turn a repair into a full replacement.

issues.t: Shudder or harsh shift from first to second gear
issues.sym: A shake or shudder as the van shifts from first to second under light or moderate throttle, or shifts that feel harsh or jerky.
issues.why: GM bulletins for this four-speed automatic describe a worn second-gear clutch causing a 1-2 shudder, and valve body wear causing harsh shifts or slipping.
issues.next: Have a transmission shop or dealer road-test it and check the fluid. Fixing a shudder early is far easier than waiting for the transmission to slip.

issues.t: ABS and traction lights on, or brakes applying by themselves
issues.sym: The ABS and traction control lights come on and may stay on. Some owners report the brakes grabbing or the van pulling to one side without pressing the pedal, or traction control kicking in at highway speed.
issues.why: Faults in the electronic brake control module, a front wheel speed sensor or the front hub that carries the sensor confuse the anti-lock and traction systems. Owners often report repeated repairs before the cause was found.
issues.next: Normal braking usually still works with the ABS light on, but if the brakes apply by themselves, stop driving and have it towed. Have the stored ABS codes read to find which sensor or module is failing.

issues.t: Brake pedal pulsation from uneven front rotors
issues.sym: The brake pedal or steering wheel pulses or vibrates when you slow down, sometimes soon after new brakes.
issues.why: The front rotors develop uneven thickness. GM issued a bulletin to correct rotor variation and fit new front brake shields on these vans.
issues.next: Have the front rotors measured. Resurfacing or replacing them, with the hub surface cleaned and lug nuts torqued evenly, usually cures it.

issues.t: Power sliding door won't close, reopens or stops working
issues.sym: The power sliding door stops partway, reverses and reopens, won't latch, or won't respond to the button or key fob.
issues.why: Worn rollers, out-of-adjustment tracks, a failing door motor or control module, or obstruction sensors cause trouble. GM published several bulletins on adjusting and repairing these doors.
issues.next: Clean and lightly lubricate the door track. If it still misbehaves, have a shop check door adjustment and the door module. Don't drive with a door that won't latch fully.

issues.t: Sliding door opening while the van is moving
issues.sym: A power sliding door unlatches or opens by itself while driving.
issues.why: An owner traced it to a failed door sensor, and federal safety regulators opened investigations into power sliding doors opening on these vans.
issues.next: If a door opens while driving, pull over safely, keep children away from it and get it inspected before carrying passengers. Use the child locks in the meantime.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or low fuel light stays on
issues.sym: The gauge shows fuel when the tank is nearly empty, won't read full after filling, or the low fuel light comes on with plenty of fuel.
issues.why: Sulfur in some gasoline corrodes the fuel level sender inside the tank, so it sends the wrong reading. GM issued a bulletin to replace the sensor.
issues.next: Track your mileage between fill-ups so you don't run out. A shop can replace the level sender, which sits in the fuel pump module.

issues.t: No-start or stalling from a wet connector under the driver's seat
issues.sym: The engine cranks but won't start, stalls while driving, or several warning lights come on at once.
issues.why: A wiring connector under the driver's seat can get wet, often from spills or leaks, and corrode. GM issued a bulletin about hard start, no start and warning lights caused by corrosion at this connector.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Ask a shop to inspect the connector under the driver's seat for moisture and green corrosion before replacing major parts.

issues.t: Intermittent no-crank or dead battery
issues.sym: Sometimes nothing happens when you turn the key, or the battery is found dead after the van sits.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for intermittent no-crank, no-start and dead battery complaints on this van, pointing to electrical faults rather than just a worn battery.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested first. If the battery is good, ask the shop to check for a parasitic drain and the starter circuit.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failed EGR valve
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often with an EGR code such as P0404. The engine may idle a little rough.
issues.why: The exhaust gas recirculation valve on the 3.5L V6 sticks or fails. The fix GM used was a replacement valve kit plus an engine computer update.
issues.next: Have the code read. It is not usually urgent, but get the valve replaced so the van passes emissions and the light can warn you of other problems.

issues.t: Whistle when accelerating from the PCV tube
issues.sym: A whistling sound from the engine when you press the gas.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation (PCV) tube on the 3.5L V6 lets air whistle through it. Replacing the tube fixes it.
issues.next: It is harmless, but a shop can swap the PCV tube if the noise bothers you.

issues.t: Engine computer chip defect (emissions recall)
issues.sym: There may be no symptom, or a check engine light related to the fuel pump or EGR system.
issues.why: Some 2005 vans had a defective chip in the engine computer, and GM replaced the computer under a voluntary emissions recall.
issues.next: Ask a Saturn-trained GM dealer to run the VIN and confirm the emissions recall was done.

issues.t: Coolant leak from crossover pipe gaskets
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping, a sweet smell after driving, or dried coolant crust on top of the engine.
issues.why: The gaskets on the coolant crossover pipe at the top of the V6 leak. GM issued a bulletin to replace them on both the 3.5L and 3.9L.
issues.next: Keep the coolant topped up with the correct coolant and watch the temperature gauge. If it starts to overheat, pull over and shut it off. Get the gaskets replaced before the leak gets worse.

issues.t: Oil leak at the oil pan or front crankshaft seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the van, oily residue on the side of the oil pan, or a burning oil smell.
issues.why: The oil pan seal and the front crankshaft (balancer) seal on these V6 engines are known to leak with age. GM issued bulletins on both.
issues.next: Check the oil level regularly and top up. Have the leak source confirmed and repaired before it soaks the belts or drips on hot exhaust parts.

issues.t: Groaning, clunk or knock when turning
issues.sym: A groan, moan, clunk or knock when you turn the steering wheel, often worse in cold weather or at low speed.
issues.why: Causes include the power steering fluid and pump in cold weather, the intermediate steering shaft and worn steering linkage. GM issued bulletins for steering noise in cold temperatures and for clunk and knock noises.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level. Have a shop find the noise source, and get it checked promptly if the steering also feels loose or stiff.

issues.t: Power steering high-pressure hose leak
issues.sym: Reddish fluid drips near the front of the engine, the power steering fluid runs low, or the steering whines and gets heavy.
issues.why: The high-pressure power steering hose on this van commonly starts to leak, often around 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Top up the fluid and get the hose replaced soon. Fluid dripping onto a hot exhaust can smoke, and running the pump dry can ruin it.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hum or wheel speed sensor fault
issues.sym: A hum or growl from a front wheel that gets louder with speed, sometimes with the ABS light on.
issues.why: The front hub and bearing assembly wears out, and the ABS wheel speed sensor is built into it, so a bad hub can also set ABS codes.
issues.next: Get it checked soon. A badly worn bearing can overheat and in extreme cases let the wheel wobble. The fix is a new hub assembly.

issues.t: Rear shocks leak or wear out
issues.sym: The rear of the van bounces or sags, or there is oily residue on the rear shocks.
issues.why: Owners report the rear shocks leaking and needing replacement, sometimes at fairly low mileage.
issues.next: Have the shocks inspected. Worn shocks make the van less stable when loaded, so replace them in pairs.

issues.t: Rear wiper stops working
issues.sym: The rear wiper won't move or stops partway.
issues.why: The rear wiper motor in the liftgate fails.
issues.next: Check the fuse first. If the fuse is fine, the motor usually needs replacing.

issues.t: OnStar loses power
issues.sym: OnStar stops working and may come back only after its fuse is pulled and replaced.
issues.why: The OnStar communication interface module fails and needs replacing.
issues.next: Note that original OnStar hardware in these vans no longer connects to today's networks, so only repair it if you rely on it.

issues.t: Horn hard to sound
issues.sym: You have to press hard on certain spots of the steering wheel pad to make the horn work.
issues.why: The springs under the horn pad are stiff. GM made softer replacement springs.
issues.next: Have a shop fit the softer springs. Be careful working near the airbag; this is not a do-it-yourself job.

issues.t: Check engine light from a loose or worn gas cap
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often after filling up, with no change in how the van drives.
issues.why: A gas cap that is loose or has a worn seal lets fuel vapor escape, which the evaporative emissions system reports as a leak.
issues.next: Tighten the cap until it clicks. If the light stays on after a few days of driving, replace the cap and have the code read.

issues.t: Parking brake may not fully release (recall)
issues.sym: After you release the parking brake, you may feel the brakes dragging and hear noise from the rear. The parking brake may also not hold the van.
issues.why: The parking brake lever mechanism could slip. GM recalled the vans to inspect the rear calipers and replace them if needed.
issues.next: Ask a GM dealer to check by VIN that recall 05V287 was completed. Recall repairs are free.

issues.t: Second-row seat latch can release in a side crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. In a severe side crash the second-row seat could come unlatched.
issues.why: The seat latch release handle on the side of the impact could be pushed and unlatch the seat. Dealers installed a protective cap.
issues.next: Ask a GM dealer to confirm recall 05V061 was done on your VIN. It is free.

issues.t: Tire and loading label shows wrong capacity (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom. The tire and loading label on the door pillar lists the wrong weight capacity.
issues.why: A misprinted label could lead owners to overload the van or set the wrong tire pressure, which can cause tire failure.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the corrected label (recall 05V552). Until then, use the load and tire pressure figures from the owner's manual.

issues.t: Some aftermarket replacement steering knuckles can break (recall)
issues.sym: No warning before failure. Applies only if a front steering knuckle was replaced with certain Dorman or NAPA aftermarket parts.
issues.why: Some aftermarket replacement knuckles sold under the Dorman OE Solutions and NAPA brands could crack in the hub area, which could cause loss of steering control.
issues.next: If your van has had front knuckle work, ask the shop which brand was used. Affected parts are replaced free under recall 09E005.
